bindings.why: On the disposable selected-stack world, a signed-in hat holder opens the real invoice. Rendered company, supplier, currency, total and zero outstanding equal the API document and the allocated USDC payment. Each rendered field has a retained screenshot and source assertion.

The posted entry's rendered party, amount, status, approval link and transaction equal its API source, the unique Payment Request and the fixture transaction. The ledger posts the amount once; screenshots are retained. This binds shows, not actions, refusals or other lifecycle states.

The actual General Ledger report renders the selected payment's Safe account, amount and posting trace. API double-entry, Trial Balance and the same-cutoff chain balance independently reconcile; a screenshot is retained.

The real Trial Balance report renders the Safe account's remaining balance. Its closing debit/credit agree with the independent API ledger sum and chain balance at the saved block cutoff; the DOM assertion and screenshot are retained.
Three actual load/replay operations each return complete fresh diagnostics with every money-path alert inactive.
Brief healthy delivery/replay stays quiet; missing diagnostics do not count as quiet.
The loaded world has no unresolved parked money issue and fresh complete operator diagnostics.
Stopping the real indexer produces exactly the expected operator-visible active alert across two polls; the test never substitutes an alert boolean.
A real unacknowledged due event held past the threshold produces one delivery alert, not an unrelated or duplicate alert.
A poisoned money event produces one operator-visible parked-money alert with a reason across successive polls.
After real indexer repair/catch-up all alerts become inactive and the original payment still reconciles without another posting.
Site delivery repair clears the observed fault; original invoice, payment posting and chain/books reconciliation still hold.
Repair/retry resolves the previously observed money fault and does not post the original payment twice.
